messages:
anya: Quick idea — for Private/VPC customers, can we expose a self-serve throttle editor in the console so they can upload per-org or per-key policies?

kevin: +1 on surface. Question: enforcement point? control plane push to dataplane vs have the dataplane pull policy from S3?

mike: I'd prefer push for faster convergence and easier audit. Push -> sidecar that applies token buckets locally. Pull adds lag and edge cases during partition.

sara: Sidecar is fine, but we need to support both per-org and per-key overrides (e.g., admin keys can bypass burst). Also retention of old policies to audit.

zach: UX note — customers will want preview/testing mode before committing. Console should run a dry-run (metrics only) for N minutes and show rejected vs allowed counts.

anya: Agreed. Proposal sketch: console UI -> validates YAML -> sends policy to control plane (private cp) -> control plane pushes to agent in customer VPC. Dry-run flag supported.

mike: Can we share the proposed policy schema here? quick mock: 
```yaml
policy_version: 1
scope: org:acme-corp
rules:
  - id: default
    type: token_bucket
    capacity: 500
    refill_per_sec: 8
    burst_capacity: 200
    targets: ["api_key", "session_id"]
  - id: admin-exempt
    type: allow_if_key_in_list
    keys: ["sk-admin-*"]
    precedence: 100
```

kevin: Nice. We should also support hierarchical precedence: per-key > per-org > default. And an explicit 'fallback' route: if quota hit, route to cheaper model or queue.

sara: About telemetry: we need token-level counters and histograms for latency when blocked vs allowed, and a per-policy change log. That will let customers see cost impact of lowering quotas.

zach: For rollout UX: console shows a canary toggle (5% traffic) and an easy rollback button. Also show the exact agent versions the policy was applied to.

ops-oncall: From ops POV, ensure emergency override in case a bad policy takes down production — a global kill-switch that bypasses customer policies for SRE keys only. Also audit who pressed it.

anya: Implementation tasks I see: 1) policy schema and validation service, 2) Console editor + dry-run graphing, 3) control plane push API, 4) lightweight agent sidecar enforcement, 5) telemetry hooks and rollout controls, 6) emergency override.

mike: One more detail: handle clock skew for token buckets. Agents should use monotonic counters and server-signed leases for refill to avoid local clock drift causing extra bursts.

kevin: Can we sketch the push API proto? small example: 
```http
POST /v1/private/policies/sync
Authorization: Bearer <cp-token>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "policy_blob": "<base64-yaml>",
  "target_agents": ["agent-1","agent-2"],
  "dry_run": true
}
```

sara: ratebot did a quick simulation (see below) — showing expected reduction in tail CPU if burst caps are enforced: 
ratebot: Simulation results — 30m run on sample workload: 98th p99 CPU down 18%, rejected requests 0.7% at new thresholds, queuing increased 1.2%. :bar_chart:

zach: Good to see numbers. We should add automated suggestions in Optimize to propose safe initial caps from observed traffic (e.g., 95th percentile * 1.2).

anya: Next steps: I'll open an RFC and a small prototype ticket. Can volunteers take tasks? mike for agent logic, kevin for push API, sara for telemetry + console charts, zach for Optimize hooks.

mike: Happy to take agent. Starting with token-bucket library and monotonic refill.

kevin: I'll start the API proto.

sara: I'll draft telemetry spec and example console graphs (dry-run heatmap + rejected list).

zach: I'll prototype the suggestion heuristic in Optimize.

ops-oncall: I'll own emergency override feature + playbook.

anya: Sweet. Posting RFC link when up. Thanks all — we'll iterate on the schema in the RFC. :thumbsup:
